findings.summary: §1.1c / 判据 2z violated on the triage path: when a triage run has exited without a dr-triage.result.v1, readResult throws ("refusing to dead-wait") instead of recording a local failure and continuing. The throw is not caught at the spawnTriage call site (src/tick-run.ts:851) and propagates to tick-entry --run, which returns exit code 2 (src/tick-entry.ts:166-176). This reproduces exactly the GT-17 failure mode the spec forbids (⛔ 不得让 tick 非零退出): one worker that exits without a result again escalates into a whole-tick failure, TICK FAILURE, and an entry-level non-zero exit. Only the generate path (src/tick-run.ts:1329-1336) was converted to record-and-continue.

判据 3 (GT-14/§1.2) and 判据 2z have no discriminative test that drives the subject. The only coverage is four unit cases over the pure predicate hasRunExited plus a source-text assertion (expect(code).toContain("export function hasRunExited")). Deleting the hasRunExited call sites from readBody/readResult — i.e. restoring the dead-wait the spec forbids — leaves every one of these tests green. No test executes --run or the wait loops, none asserts the tick still exits 0 with the diagnostic present in output, and the required reverse case (bus unreachable ⇒ tick must still exit non-zero) is absent. This is the anti-pattern the spec records as having caused 3 prior rejections (§5, GT-23).

判据 2b (GT-15/GT-16 regression) is entirely absent: no test drives a real `--run` on a seed board (1 clue) and asserts the elapsed time is below half of the engine's workflow.yaml limits.node_timeout with termination readable. There is no timing measurement of any kind under test/ (no elapsed/duration/hrtime assertion anywhere), so raising node_timeout to 1800 is unaccompanied by the required proof that a seed-board tick stays far below the engine cap; the cap change is currently the only thing standing between the tick and the guillotine.

判据 2a (GT-19) has no discriminative test that drives the entry. The shipped test only regex-scrapes three numbers out of profiles/deploy/e0-regression.env and compares them (maxAttempts > wallClock/backoff); it never executes bin/e0-regression.sh, never constructs the required situation (wall-clock budget still available but attempt count exhausted ⇒ the entry must continue), and would stay green if the entry's limit logic were reverted to attempt-count-primary. Note the loop still evaluates the attempt limit before the wall-clock limit (bin/e0-regression.sh:383-412); only the profile's 40-vs-20 arithmetic keeps attempts from binding first, and nothing under test protects that ordering.

判据 4b regression not met: MAX_CLUES is not declared by any profile and is not wired through fleet.yaml.tpl / workflow.yaml (no occurrence of MAX_CLUES anywhere in the tree; the tick seed payload wires only max_writes/triage_threshold). The describe block advertising this coverage ("MAX_CLUES by profile") asserts MAX_WRITES=96 instead — a different key — so the required narrowing of the regression baseline (also the stated route to 判据 6/Z1 self-consistency between the ~3h convergence time and the profile's declared 2400s wall clock) is neither delivered nor tested.

The `timings` staged instrumentation that the spec lists as an already-correct, non-regressible deliverable (⛔ 保留：timings 覆盖整个 tick，含 generate 段) does not exist anywhere in the delivered tree — there is no `timings` or `totalMs` field in src/, scripts/, bin/ or test/. §1.1 requires the node_timeout value to be justified by that per-stage measurement, and GT-21 requires the delivery to be able to point at the field/run/file each number came from; the delivery instead reuses only the dispatcher's GT-13 figure and ships no instrumentation to re-measure.

§1.2 requires the exited-without-result diagnostic to name run_id, role AND the already-waited duration. Both diagnostics name run_id and role but omit the elapsed wait time, so the record cannot show whether the read stopped immediately or waited most of the 15-minute budget — which is precisely the property the requirement exists to make observable.

On the generate path, an exited-without-result run makes readBody return an empty string, which spawnGenerateRole hands back as `{ body: "" }` and the doc pipeline consumes as an ordinary body. Nothing marks that doc/clue as failed, so a local failure is silently folded into an apparently successful generation — §1.1c forbids both silence and treating it as success (⛔ 该条 clue/doc 的状态要如实反映失败).

The measured-max constant is named MEASURED_MAX_MS but holds 904.2 seconds. The comparisons are unit-consistent (both sides are seconds, so the assertion is correct), but the name asserts milliseconds and invites a future 1000x error in exactly the arithmetic this package exists to fix.

Declared headroom is inconsistent between artifacts: workflow.yaml states `1800 / 904.2 ≈ 2.0×` while the test asserts the ratio is ≥ 1.99 (the true value is 1.9907). Since 判据 2 requires node_timeout ≥ measured max × the declared multiplier, the declared multiplier and the asserted one should be the same number.

The single blocker carried over from the previous package's final review is genuinely fixed: limits.node_timeout is now 1800s (> the 904.2s measured max, ~1.99× headroom, and > DEFAULT_AGENT_RESULT_TIMEOUT_MS/1000 so the engine guillotine sits after a legal wait budget), the arithmetic is spelled out in the comment, and 判据 2's assertion is now made against the recorded measured max rather than against a source constant, with a discriminant that reddens if the value is dialled back toward 30.

Both wait loops now issue a full paginated read of board:agent-runs on every poll iteration (default every 3s) in addition to the result read, roughly doubling bus I/O while waiting. Since §1.1b requires a seed-board tick to stay far below the engine cap, consider checking exit status on a coarser cadence or reusing the messages already fetched by the result read.
